reviews.review: It's really good. The Nightweaver is driving me insane

I've tried my absolute best to like this game but I just don't. This game does meta game progression / secrets / gunplay / classes and weapon variety very well, but it does so much more wrong.

[list]
[*]The character feels insanely stiff, making combat very clunky. Getting hit once is almost a death sentence because it's nearly impossible to get away from enemies and you'll get stunlocked if enemies surround you. This sucks even harder on boss fights that summon adds.
[*]The level designs are extremely poor and are so maze-like. This game is the ultimate "where the ♥♥♥♥ am I supposed to go?" simulator.
[*]Boss fights vary from "Okay that was pretty cool" to "What the ♥♥♥♥ whoever designed this needs to be shot"
[*]Literally everything is cryptic and barely explained. This game requires you to be checking the Wiki constantly because the game is nearly impossible to play without it. Pretty much every area, item, and mechanic is a puzzle with vague hints of what to do.
[*]Maps feel like a chore to walk through, especially if you're trying to figure out where the hell you're supposed to be going. The minimap doesn't even have cardinal directions on them so it's possible to accidentally end up walking south when you really meant to be walking north.
[*]Everything in this game feels [i]slow[/i]. Using items and consumables feels like a challenge because your animations are slower than enemies attacks, so you will get interrupted if you don't time them just right. The same goes with reloading guns.
[*]There are many unlocks that are available only through multiplayer mechanics. If you don't have anyone to play with to specifically aim for them, there are some things you won't be able to get.
[*]Ammo starvation is real. If you're on a big map or during some boss fights, it's entirely possible to run out of ammo. There are consumables to restore it (which as I said above, consumables take forever to use) and you can get ammo drops, but it's pure RNG if that happens.
[*]Replayability is questionable. When you start a new campaign or adventure mode, it's a dice roll of which version of the map you roll and the optional dungeons are also always random. If you're hunting for a specific armor / ring / weapon / amulet, you'll basically need to keep rolling the dice over and over until you get the map you want. The main areas and boss fights stay the same, so it can become repetitive quickly.
[/list]

Again, I want to like this game, but I feel exhausted playing it and at one point even asked myself "Am I even having fun right now?", which I could honestly answer "No, I'm not", so I turned it off and wrote this review after uninstalling it. It is possible to enjoy, and even love this game, but you are going to need a large amount of patience in order to do so.

If you enjoy the *Dark Souls* formula blended with shooter mechanics and appreciate stunning environments created with Unreal Engine 5 (especially if you use the DLSS 5 mod to push the visuals to the absolute limit) then this game is a true marvel. 

Beyond its technical excellence, my experience with the multiplayer community has been fantastic!

I was lucky enough to encounter extraordinary players who showed immense patience, helped me acquire excellent weapons, and supported me in taking on the toughest bosses.

In my personal experience, Remnant 2 offered a spectacular balance of replayability, graphical fidelity, and a welcoming community.

I'm certain that if you enjoy the genre, you will enjoy this game.
